item.title: [Itrfoundation] Benchmarking: One of the Most Valuable Tools School Boards Aren’t Using
item.description:
Benchmarking helps school boards make better decisions by comparing their district with true peer districts—not just nearby schools or statewide averages. Comparing districts with similar enrollment and student needs provides a more meaningful basis for evaluating staffing, spending, and student outcomes. The goal isn’t to copy another district—it’s to ask better questions. Benchmarking identifies differences in performance and resource allocation, helping school boards investigate what is working well and where improvements may be needed. As enrollment declines and financial pressures grow, objective comparisons become even more important. Tools like ITR Foundation’s School District Report Card help school boards and taxpayers evaluate how effectively districts are using limited resources to improve student outcomes.

The post Benchmarking: One of the Most Valuable Tools School Boards Aren’t Using appeared first on ITR Foundation.

item.description:
Immigration is one of those issues where Washington seems determined to make everyone angry while solving almost nothing.

Many Americans have real concerns. They worry about too many people coming too quickly, wages being pressured, schools and hospitals being strained, housing becoming less affordable, and cultural trust weakening in communities that already feel stretched.

Those concerns should not be dismissed. A serious country, like a constitutional republic, must have borders, law, order, and accountability. But we should also remember something too often lost in today’s debate: immigration has been one of America’s greatest sources of strength.
